title: Clean the usernames
scenario: Clean up the usernames: strip the stray spaces off each one.

intro.job: Clean up the usernames: strip the stray spaces off each one.

idea.rule: Strings never change in place — a method hands you a NEW string. Catch it or lose it.
idea.detail: A string can't be edited. name.strip() doesn't change name — it builds a brand-new string with the spaces gone and hands it back. If nothing catches it with an =, that new string is gone the moment the line ends, and name is exactly what it was.

model_restatement: Make a new list with every name cleaned of its spaces.

clarify.question: What if there are no names?
Could a name already be clean?
clarify.answer: Some already are — the clean ones stay clean.

clarify.question: Should I change names, or build a new list?
clarify.answer: Build a new list of clean names — leave names as it is.

clarify.question: Any spaces inside the names?
clarify.answer: No — just the spaces on the ends.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: For each name: clean the spaces off it and add it to the clean list. Print the clean list.
draft_code:
clean = []
for name in names:
    tag = name
    tag.strip()
    clean.append(tag)
print(clean)

checkpoints.prompt: Iteration 1: right after line 4 (tag.strip()), what is tag?
After line 5 in iteration 1, what is clean?
With the fix — after line 4 in iteration 1, what is clean?

why_line: tag.strip() builds a new string 'ana' and hands it back — but nothing catches it, so tag is still ' ana '.

explain.rule: tag.strip() is a photocopier: it hands you a cleaned copy — and if nobody catches the copy, it falls on the floor while tag stays ' ana '.
explain.bridge: So how do you catch the copy .strip() hands you?

fix.rule: name.strip() makes a new, cleaned string — tag = catches it before it's lost.

walk.gloss: An empty list for the clean names.
Make the cleaned copy and catch it in tag.
Add the caught tag to the list.

fix.recommended:
clean = []
for name in names:
    tag = name.strip()
    clean.append(tag)
print(clean)

alternatives.code:
clean = []
for name in names:
    tag = name
    tag = tag.strip()
    clean.append(tag)
print(clean)
alternatives.note: Catch it in two steps — the same fix, closest to the draft.

alternatives.code:
clean = [name.strip() for name in names]
print(clean)
alternatives.note: The shortcut — once you can trace the long way.

hints: After line 4 runs, what is tag?
.strip() hands back a new string — and nothing catches it.

checkpoint.prompt: With one-sided spaces, what gets printed?

follow_up.recommended:

for name in names:

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — strip() takes spaces off both ends, even when only one end has them.

one_liner: Strings never change in place — a method hands you a NEW string. Catch it or lose it.
